summary: Both findings verified at their evidence and confirmed: /1 (medium, owner of the height-one intersection theorem) and /2 (low, understated library note on the fundamental equality). /1: route 7 and the route 4 brief put Krull's theorem (normal noetherian domain = intersection of its height-one localizations, Matsumura 11.5(ii), used only in Proposition 5.1, p. 16) and its two associated-prime lemmas under AutomorphicCongruences:L4, which requires L3 and KatoEulerSystems:L4 and, on the production graph (scripts.build.assemble, require_distances=False, at 24bcb8e8), has 846 ancestor stages in 120 roadmaps; DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3 has 5 in 2 and, as narrowed by the accepted RS-08, keeps 'associated-prime and support lemmas'. The brief's 'early algebraic portion of L4' is not a stage, so the Part II would inherit all of L4's prerequisites. Scope correction to the red team's fix: pick R03.3 (not 'R03.3 or A0-extension'), and krull-intersection becomes status missing routed to R03.3 (R03.3's text does not name the theorem, so 'planned: R03.3' would overstate it); L4's own import and the PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4 / FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.1 imports are maintainer notes, not fixer edits. /2: Tau Ceti f790474 has TauCeti.Place.sum_ramificationIdx_mul_relativeDegree_eq_finrank (AffineModel/Extension.lean:293), the fundamental identity at every place of a finite chart for Dedekind models R, S with Module.Finite R S and no separability instance; the item note's 'the pin supplies only the separable function-field wrapper' is false as a library claim, and route 3's reason both assigns and disclaims the equality. Status 'planned' (AlgebraicCurves Layer 6) stays.

sources.citation: Dittmann–Pop, Characterizing finitely generated fields by a single field axiom, arXiv 2012.01307v2 (final author version, 19 pp.), the version recorded by the extraction and the red team; hash matches. Read Lemma 3.6 (p. 10) and Proposition 5.1 (p. 16). The published version is Ann. of Math. 198 (2023), no. 3, 1203–1227, doi 10.4007/annals.2023.198.3.4; neither finding quotes a stated result, so no collation against it was needed.

Libraries at the pinned baseline: Mathlib 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174 and Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369, read through the baseline declaration index and the source files at those commits.

findings.reason: Checked at every locator. The paper uses the theorem once, in the proof of Proposition 5.1 (p. 16 of arXiv v2): 'S = ⋂_{p∈X¹} S_p, see e.g. [Ma], Thm 11.5, (ii)'. The extraction routes krull-intersection (planned: AutomorphicCongruences:L4), principal-associated-height-one and associated-localization-detection (both missing) to AutomorphicCongruences:L4 (route 7), and the route 4 brief says 'Import the general height-one intersection theorem from the early algebraic portion of … (AutomorphicCongruences:L4)'. In data/atlas.json L4 ('Integral descent and specialization') requires AutomorphicCongruences:L3 and KatoEulerSystems:L4; AUDIT-23 (data/library-coverage.json) lists the target 'an element integral at every height-one prime of a normal noetherian domain is integral' as partial. I re-ran scripts.build.assemble(require_distances=False) read-only at 24bcb8e8: L4 has 846 ancestor stages in 120 roadmaps (KatoEulerSystems among them); DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3 and AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:A0-extension have 5 each, in 2 roadmaps (R03.1, R03.2 and three ModularCurves anchors; R09.1–R09.4 and ModularCurves 0C). The atlas links whole stages, so 'the early algebraic portion of L4' cannot be expressed and the FinitelyGeneratedFieldDefinability Part II would become downstream of L4's whole ancestry, which violates §15's 'plan it once … in the roadmap that owns it: usually the most foundational one'. The other consumers are real: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/bidual-intersection takes A = ⋂_{𝔭∈P(A)} A_𝔭 as a hypothesis, and FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.1/tate-generic-fibre-theorem uses 'R = ⋂ R_𝔭 over height-one primes' as its reduction step. At the pins the general theorem is absent: Mathlib has only IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.iInf_localization_eq_bot (RingTheory/DedekindDomain/Ideal/Lemmas.lean:564) and the valuation-ring form Subring.eq_iInf_of_isIntegrallyClosedIn (Valuation/LocalSubring.lean:199); Tau Ceti has no Krull-domain declaration. R03.3 ('Give equidimensionality, associated-prime and support lemmas for finite modules'), as narrowed by the accepted RS-08, keeps exactly these associated-prime lemmas and is the right owner; A0-extension ('higher-dimensional moduli prerequisites') mentions neither associated primes nor this theorem, and the extraction already moved the item off it, so it is not an equal alternative. Adversarial check on the red team: its fix says 'keep the missing/planned statuses' and offers A0-extension as an option; both are corrected below. Medium severity is right: no statement is false, but a prerequisite link changes. Authorised fix, in research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-DITTMANN-POP-23.result.json and the matching text of PAPER-DITTMANN-POP-23.md only: (a) route 7 becomes a source route to roadmap DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra, stages ['DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3'], with the same three items, and a reason saying that R03.3 owns the general associated-prime and height-one algebra, has no automorphic prerequisites, and that AutomorphicCongruences:L4 imports the theorem; (b) krull-intersection: status 'missing', remove its 'planned' field, and replace the note ('The reviewed AUDIT-23 target at L4 … Removed from the A0-extension route …') by one saying the general theorem is owned by R03.3 through route 7 and that the L4 audit target is the same statement, which L4 imports; principal-associated-height-one and associated-localization-detection stay missing; (c) route 3 reason: 'The height-one intersection theorem imports AutomorphicCongruences:L4' becomes '… imports DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3'; (d) route 4 brief: replace the sentence importing from 'the early algebraic portion of … (AutomorphicCongruences:L4)' by 'Import the general height-one intersection theorem for normal noetherian domains, with its associated-prime lemmas, from Commutative algebra for deformation theory and patching (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3).'; (e) gap DP23-G5's remaining text and the report's 'Earlier ownership remains intact' paragraph: L4 becomes R03.3. Maintainer notes in the fix report, not fixer edits: AutomorphicCongruences:L4 keeps only its zeta-element descent and imports the general theorem from R03.3; PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4 and FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.1 import it from R03.3; the route 7 verdict in PAPER-DITTMANN-POP-23.review.json is superseded by this verdict and is not rewritten by the fixer.

Read at Tau Ceti f790474: TauCeti.Place.sum_ramificationIdx_mul_relativeDegree_eq_finrank (TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/AffineModel/Extension.lean:293) proves ∑_{P'∈s} e(P'|P)·f(P'|P) = finrank F F' at the place of every height-one prime 𝔭 of an affine model R, for an affine model S of F'/k' over R. Its section variables are [IsDedekindDomain R], [IsDedekindDomain S], the fraction-field and scalar-tower instances, [Algebra.IsIntegral F F'] and [Module.Finite R S] (line 224); there is no separability instance, and the module docstring calls it the fundamental identity (Stichtenoth 3.1.11) at a place of the finite chart. The separable global wrapper is sum_ramificationIdx_mul_relativeDegree_eq_finrank_of_isSeparable (Place/Extension/Fundamental.lean:77, [Algebra.IsSeparable F F'] at line 61), and the inequality is sum_ramificationIdx_mul_relativeDegree_le_finrank (Place/Extension/Fibre.lean:300). So the item note's 'The pin supplies only the separable function-field wrapper' is a false library claim at the pin. I re-derived the use in Lemma 3.6 (p. 10): K ⊃ K_s are function fields in one variable over k_1(u) with K|K_s purely inseparable; taking R and S as the integral closures of k_1(u)[u_d] in K_s and K (and of k_1(u)[u_d⁻¹] for places at infinity), finite-normalization-generic with A = k_1(u) makes both finite over the polynomial ring, hence S finite over R and both Dedekind, and the chart identity applies. Finiteness is genuinely needed (the identity fails for non-Japanese DVRs), so finite Dedekind models are the one remaining input and the status 'planned' with owner AlgebraicCurves Layer 6 stays. Route 3's reason does say the equality 'also belongs here: it follows from the separability-free finite normalization this layer owns …' and then that it 'is imported, not assigned to this source route'; the item note ('Do not route a second proof to A0-extension') settles it. Low severity is right. Authorised fix, in PAPER-DITTMANN-POP-23.result.json and the matching .md text only: in function-field-fundamental-equality, replace the sentence 'The pin supplies only the separable function-field wrapper; Mathlib supplies the finite-flat algebra identity.' by a citation of tauceti:TauCeti.Place.sum_ramificationIdx_mul_relativeDegree_eq_finrank (finite-chart identity, no separability, needs Dedekind models with S finite over R), tauceti:TauCeti.Place.sum_ramificationIdx_mul_relativeDegree_le_finrank and the separable wrapper, and say that the remaining input is a finite Dedekind model in the purely inseparable case (finite-normalization-generic); add the first two declarations to the item's 'library' list (status stays 'planned', planned stays AlgebraicCurves Layer 6, as for the other planned items that cite library support); rewrite the second proof step to apply the Tau Ceti chart identity to those models instead of re-deriving it from Ideal.sum_ramification_inertia_eq_finrank. In route 3's reason delete the sentence beginning 'The fundamental equality for one-variable function fields without separability … also belongs here' and keep the following sentence.
